title: Algo + AI trading platform for every trader is now live for early users (no coding/technical knowledge needed)
author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
selftext:
A few weeks ago I shared while25 here and got a lot of great feedback. Thank you for that. It's now live for early users, and you can try it today.

I traded with four disconnected tools. TradingView for charts, my broker's platform for orders, Claude for analysis and VS Code for writing code. So I built While25 to put all four on one screen. It's meant to be the only platform a trader needs.

**Here's how it works:**

**Charts**: All the standard indicators and drawing tools, with several charts side by side. You place and manage orders right on the chart.

**Python** **and** **AI**: Custom indicators, strategies and backtests in Python, for any idea you have. The AI assistant reads your charts and positions and writes the code for you. It can't place trades.

**Orders**: Stocks, ETFs, futures and options from one order screen, including multi-leg options. Positions, orders and fills sit in one order book. Every order routes straight to your broker.

**Risk**: You set a max loss per session, a max order size and a max number of orders. Every order is checked against them before it goes out, whether you sent it or your code did.

**News and fundamentals**: News comes from Google. Fundamentals come from Yahoo Finance. Other data vendors can be plugged in.

**Good to know:**

Desktop app for Mac and Windows.

Connects to **Interactive Brokers**, **Alpaca**, **Zerodha and Upstox**. Coinbase, Binance and Robinhood are coming next.

Your funds and broker keys never touch our servers.

Download it here: [https://www.while25.com/download](https://www.while25.com/download)

Try it and tell me what's missing. I read every comment.

comments.author: spoidercide
comments.body:
PSA: RED FLAGS TO LOOK OUT FOR AND QUESTIONS TO ASK WHENEVER YOU SEE THIS KIND OF THING:

whats your business model here? how are we supposed to trust it without a git upload?

if there's no pricing, roadmap, or open source how or why should anyone assume its not predatory?

it could be as simple as getting others strategies collected

it could be a fee system.

but the ambiguity with on the surface a nice looking dash is very sketchy imo

its almost free to make a website an executable and have a .com these days

a free tier of claude could get it done in 10 minutes.

this seems more nefarious than a rugpull

posts like these are easily capable of farming your credentials without multiple user review or trustpilot scoring from actual coders.

replies.author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
replies.body:
There's gonna be pricing and we do have roadmap. One thing we dont have is open-source git repo because making it open-source will add burden for us to stay away from the AI slop.

while25 is running completely locally on your machine and your API key, orders and portfolio never comes to us. We write that confidently on our site as well! 

The things we openly claim in financial app has to be real otherwise anyone can sue us and we are quite aware of that.

Roadmap: we are adding more brokers like coinbase, kraken, Charles Schwab, etc next.

If with all your support we are getting traction and based on traction funding we will provide proprietary data from our servers it self.

I hope this answers your question!

replies.body:
“*One thing we* *dont* *have* *is* *open-source git repo because making it open-source will* *add* *burden for us to stay away from the AI slop.*”

replies.author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
replies.body:
Open source means everyone can contribute and which means someone has to do gatekeeping on what changes are coming in. We are currently 2 people working on this and we do not have bandwidth to manage one more thing.

One more obvious thing is we also want to protect our ip that we have developed so far for making it compatible with all sorts of market, assets and brokers along with native python coding environment.

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body: For the session-loss and order-count controls, does the risk state persist across an app restart and reconcile with orders placed directly in the broker's own terminal? A useful demo would be: hit a limit, restart While25, reconnect, and show that a new order is still blocked for the same session. I would also want the UI to show which broker positions are included in that limit and the timezone used for the reset.

replies.author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
replies.body:
Great question and one of the complex thing usually no one builds.

We do reconcile external orders and their PnL well and if once the session PnL is hit even after restart you cant place the order, your execution engine will be completely locked until you reset the limit and re arm session PnL.

Because we work with multiple global market we cant have single timezone so we have given this liberty to user so it can reset the PnL whenever he wants. You can keep the session running for 2 days also its up to you. 

The only thing we cant do is, stopping you place external order after session limit hit. Because we can only stop you trading from while25!
